196:    * Existing bindings are left untouched (the Binding table keeps the
197:    * history); this only prevents the disabled agent from being (re)started.
198:    * The read is a synchronous in-memory lookup (the definition is loaded
199:    * once at construction) — no config/database I/O on the message hot path.
200:    * @param {string} agentId
201:    * @throws {Error} code `AGENT_NOT_FOUND` (unknown) or `AGENT_DISABLED`.
202:    */
203:   function assertRunnable(agentId) {
204:     assertRecoveryAdmission(reconciliationStore, agentId)
205:     const defined = agentDefinition.getAgent(agentId) // throws AGENT_NOT_FOUND when unknown
206:     if (defined.disabled === true) {
207:       throw Object.assign(new Error(`agent-router: agent ${agentId} is disabled (not runnable)`), { code: 'AGENT_DISABLED' })
208:     }
268:   /** Spawn + initialize one generation for an installed STARTUP slot. */
269:   async function startProcessForSlot(agentId, entry) {
270:     // F-1 (C-008 no-child discipline): every synchronous pre-spawn
271:     // preparation step is failure-converged — a throw settles the shared
272:     // startup promise exactly once and cleans the exact STARTUP slot to
273:     // EMPTY via identity CAS (no REAP, no shutdown write, no kill; the next
274:     // ensureRunning retries; stale first-generation cleanups are audit-only).
275:     let workspace
276:     let home
277:     let processConfig
278:     try {
279:       entry.startupFailureStage = 'resolveWorkspace'
280:       // workspace-bootstrap is the single owner of the agentId -> workspace /
281:       // DSH_HOME mapping (D-002 boundary). The router only decides WHEN to
282:       // start the agent, not where its home lives — so it calls the service
283:       // without any root override.
284:       workspace = workspaceBootstrap.resolveWorkspace(agentId)
285:       entry.startupFailureStage = 'resolveDshHome'
286:       home = workspaceBootstrap.resolveDshHome(agentId)
287:       entry.startupFailureStage = 'resolveProcessConfig'
288:       // Route-chain spawns freeze the wanted route's process config onto the
289:       // slot at turn-start snapshot time (parent CTR-007); legacy spawns keep
290:       // resolving the default route here (process-boundary re-read only).
291:       processConfig = entry.spawnConfig?.processConfig ?? resolveProcessConfig(agentId) ?? {}
292:       // DEC-IMPL-004 reuse identity: recorded on the slot so the route gate
293:       // can compare later attempts against this process's frozen route.
294:       entry.routeIdentity = entry.spawnConfig?.routeIdentity ?? canonicalRouteIdentity(processConfig)
295:       // Provision the agent home (settings/credentials/profile/plugin farm)
296:       // and the workspace directory — idempotent. The provisioning is driven
297:       // by cfg.agentProfile: whatever profile this router spawns must be
298:       // fully installed HERE, so a fresh Agent works without any external
299:       // pre-provisioning (FIX 1).
300:       entry.startupFailureStage = 'provisionHome'
301:       provisionHome(home, workspace, {
302:         profile: cfg.agentProfile,
303:         ...(processConfig.subscription === undefined ? {} : { subscription: processConfig.subscription }),
304:         // The runtime's own deployment root pins the shared credentialFile
305:         // reference to THIS surface's canonical store — a foreign domain's
306:         // lineage (or a per-home drift path) fails loud in provisioning
307:         // instead of ever reaching a child (FLEET_SHARED_CODEX_AUTH A2/A4).
308:         deploymentRoot: resolveProductionRoot(cfg.productionRoot),
309:       })
320:     let proc
321:     try {
322:       entry.startupFailureStage = 'processFactory'
323:       proc = processFactory({
324:         agentId,
325:         home,
326:         workspace,
327:         profile: cfg.agentProfile,
328:         provider: processConfig.provider,
329:         model: processConfig.model,
330:         providerEnv: processConfig.providerEnv,
331:         omitEnv: processConfig.omitEnv,
332:         log,
333:         // The per-agent process must know its own identity: the memory plugin
334:         // and the switch tool resolve agentId from $DSH_AGENT_ID when set.
335:         // DSH_PRIMARY_WORKSPACE (AGENT_PRIMARY_WORKSPACE_IMPORT_V1 §4) is the
336:         // SAME mechanical pass-through: the control plane's already-resolved
337:         // primary workspace (resolveWorkspace output above — the single path
338:         // authority). The Router only hands the value to the child process's
339:         // session-less memory resolution; it never re-derives the path and
340:         // never branches on it.
341:         env: { DSH_AGENT_ID: agentId, DSH_PRIMARY_WORKSPACE: workspace },
342:         // V2 lifecycle wiring: monotonic generation, the static per-Agent
343:         // resolved deadline config (immutable for this process), the shared
344:         // Router reconciliation store and the identity-CAS slot integration.
345:         processGeneration: entry.generation,
346:         deadlines: deadlineConfig.perAgent(agentId),
347:         reconciliationStore,
348:         registryIntegration,
349:       })
350:     } catch (cause) {
351:       throw failStartupSlotNoChild(agentId, entry, cause)
352:     }
353:     entry.processRef = proc
354:     // DSH tool relay: a per-agent process asks the Control Plane to run a
355:     // Router domain operation (switch) or a trusted Broker capability call
356:     // (broker). The tool itself owns no policy — it forwards the request;
357:     // every decision happens in the Router (parent-rpc-relay.js).
358:     proc.onRpcRequest = createParentRpcHandler({
359:       agentId,
360:       log,
361:       getProc: () => proc,
362:       getBrokerGateway,
363:       switchAgent,
364:     })
